# GEO report: Millstone Bakery **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 100/100, Strong Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points). How it's calculated: low = 23 ÷ 23 × 100 = 100. High = (23 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 100. This is a small static HTML site with four pages. Every applicable rule is Clear when read from the code. The only things the code can't settle are what the server and any CDN do when real crawlers visit. These results are "read from code", not measured on a live site. ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first Nothing is broken, so there's no fix to make. The biggest open question is outside the code. ### 1. Confirm real crawlers get through your host or CDN - **Why it matters:** Code can't show whether a firewall or CDN (content delivery network) blocks search crawlers even though `robots.txt` allows them. - **Where:** `robots.txt:1` - **What the code says:** `User-agent: *` followed by `Allow: /` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 100 if it comes back clear. 100 if it comes back a problem, because the code score covers only the code, so this check would show up as a live finding. A live scan would give a separate live score. ### 2. Optional: add the Worth considering ideas below These are small content and markup improvements. They don't change the score. ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt is reachable and valid | Clear | `robots.txt:1-8`, plain text with valid lines | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers have the access your policy says | Clear | `robots.txt:1-3` allows all except `/members/`. Policy is `aiSearchCrawlers: allow`. `GPTBot` is blocked at line 6, which matches `trainingCrawlers: block` | | GEO-014 | Sitemap-listed and linked routes are indexable | Clear | 3 of 3 public routes have no noindex. `members/index.html:9` is noindex on purpose and isn't in the sitemap | | GEO-015 | Absolute canonical on the declared origin | Clear | 4 of 4 pages have an absolute canonical on `https://www.millstonebakery.example` | | GEO-003 | Main content is in server HTML | Clear | Plain static HTML with no client rendering | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | No `application/ld+json` or `"@type"` found anywhere | | GEO-011 | Valid sitemap is discoverable | Clear | `sitemap.xml:3-5`, referenced at `robots.txt:8` with an absolute URL | | GEO-012 | Title, description and html lang | Clear | All 4 pages have `lang="en"`, a unique title and a unique description | | GEO-016 | Routes reachable through server-rendered links | Clear | `` navigation on every page, for example `index.html:12` | | GEO-017 | Snippet restrictions don't conflict with the AI-search policy | Clear | Only a scoped `data-nosnippet` at `breads.html:16`, which is deliberate. No page-wide `nosnippet` | | GEO-002 | Selected accessibility checks | Clear | The one image (`index.html:16`) has alt text. All links have text and every page has a title. I read all 4 pages | | GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | No app declared | | GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only) | Not scored | None present | | GEO-102 | App structured data (information only) | Not scored | Not an app | ## Other problems found None found. ## Worth considering Optional ideas. They aren't problems, and they don't change the score. - **Add business details people would ask for:** `index.html:15`: `Pre-order for weekend collection.` There's no address, opening hours, phone number or way to pre-order anywhere in the text. Adding them, ideally on a visible contact or visit section, might help readers and machines. - **Label the bakery with structured data:** the home page has no JSON-LD. Once the address and hours are on the page, a `Bakery` (or `LocalBusiness`) block with name, address, hours and URL could label facts that are already visible. - **Back up the loaf claim:** `breads.html:15`: `Over twenty loaves through the week, including our seeded rye and the country white.` Only two loaves are named. A list of the loaves, or a page per loaf, would give the claim something to stand on. - **Say how to book classes:** `classes.html:15`: `Book early, because places go quickly.` There's no link or form, and no price, date, class length or group size. Adding those answers what a visitor would come to ask. - **Add `` to the sitemap:** `sitemap.xml:3`: `https://www.millstonebakery.example/`. None of the entries has a date. Real modified dates help crawlers decide what to revisit. - **Add social sharing tags:** `index.html:6-8`. There are no `og:title`, `og:description` or `og:image` tags. They control how pages look when shared. - **Put the allergen information in the page text as well:** `breads.html:16`: `

Contains gluten. Ask us about allergens.

`. Keeping it out of snippets is a deliberate choice. If you want more allergen detail, add it as normal text on the page. ## Can't tell from code - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs `, which checks real crawlers against their published addresses. - **GEO-013, GEO-011 and GEO-014 live behaviour:** whether `/robots.txt` and the sitemap URLs actually answer 200, and whether any `X-Robots-Tag` header is set by the host. These are live-only checks and don't change the code results. - **The image file:** `/img/loaves.jpg` (`index.html:16`) isn't in this repository. It may be deployed separately, so check that it exists. ## Assumptions - You want search and AI-search tools to find this site, as `geo.config.json` says (`aiSearchCrawlers: allow`). Blocking the training crawler `GPTBot` is treated as deliberate. - I read `geo.config.json`, `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml` and all 4 HTML pages (`index.html`, `breads.html`, `classes.html`, `members/index.html`). That is every file in the repository, with no JSON-LD sources and no build or framework layer. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command if you'd like help with the optional ideas above. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
